record.paper_title: Kirby diagrams, trisections and gems of PL 4-manifolds: relationships, results and open problems
record.original_question: Which classes of gems force the trisections obtained from them to realize the actual trisection genus of the represented 4-manifold? This asks for a characterization of 5-colored graph encodings for which the trisection arising either directly as a gem-induced trisection, or indirectly by first taking a compact manifold with connected boundary and then capping off by the canonical 4-dimensional handlebody, is genus-minimizing.

evidence.quote: With respect to Section 3.2, a fundamental problem involves the possible characterization of classes of gems so that the arising trisections (either directly, as gem-induced trisections, or indirectly, via the approach described in Section 3.2.2) realize the trisection genus of the represented 4-manifolds.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

(1) A gem (graph-encoded manifold) of a closed connected PL 4-manifold M is a 5-colored graph (Γ, γ): that is, a finite multigraph Γ = (V(Γ), E(Γ)) which is regular of degree 5, together with an edge-coloring γ : E(Γ) → Δ₄ := {0, 1, 2, 3, 4} such that any two edges sharing a vertex receive distinct colors. To such a colored graph one associates a pseudo-complex K(Γ) by taking a 4-simplex σ_v for each vertex v ∈ V(Γ), labeling the vertices of σ_v by the elements of Δ₄, and identifying, for each edge e ∈ E(Γ) of color c joining v and v', the two (3-dimensional) faces of σ_v and σ_{v'} opposite to the vertex labeled c, via the unique label-preserving simplicial isomorphism. The graph (Γ, γ) is called a gem of M when |K(Γ)| is PL-homeomorphic to M.

(2) A (g; k₁, k₂, k₃)-trisection of a closed connected oriented PL 4-manifold M is a decomposition M = X₁ ∪ X₂ ∪ X₃ such that:
   • each X_i is diffeomorphic to the boundary-connected sum ♮^{k_i}(S¹ × B³);
   • each pairwise intersection X_i ∩ X_j (i ≠ j) is a 3-dimensional handlebody of genus g;
   • the triple intersection X₁ ∩ X₂ ∩ X₃ is a closed orientable surface Σ_g of genus g.
The trisection genus 𝔤(M) of M is the minimum integer g such that M admits a (g; k₁, k₂, k₃)-trisection for some non-negative integers k₁, k₂, k₃ ≤ g.

(3) From any gem (Γ, γ) of M one may construct a trisection T(Γ, γ) of M by either of the following two procedures:
   (a) the direct gem-induced trisection, obtained from a suitable partition of the colors of Γ into three blocks and the associated regular neighborhoods of subcomplexes of K(Γ);
   (b) the indirect construction, in which one first uses (Γ, γ) to produce a compact PL 4-manifold with connected boundary, and then caps the boundary off by the canonical 4-dimensional handlebody to obtain a closed M together with an induced trisection.

Each of these constructions yields a trisection whose genus g(Γ, γ) is determined combinatorially by (Γ, γ), and one has g(Γ, γ) ≥ 𝔤(M).

Problem. Characterize the classes 𝒞 of 5-colored graphs (Γ, γ) with the property that, for every (Γ, γ) ∈ 𝒞 representing a closed PL 4-manifold M, the associated trisection T(Γ, γ) — produced either by the direct construction (a) or by the indirect construction (b) — is genus-minimizing, i.e. satisfies g(Γ, γ) = 𝔤(M).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is explicitly posed as a fundamental open question regarding which gems yield genus-minimizing trisections, and no published characterization has been found. Recent works on relationships among gems, Kirby diagrams, and trisections discuss bounds (e.g., regular genus vs. trisection genus) but no full characterization.

status_evidence.title: Kirby diagrams, trisections and gems of PL 4-manifolds (zbMATH listing)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing relationships between gems, Kirby diagrams, and trisections, listing open problems on genus-minimizing gem-induced trisections.
status_evidence.claim: The characterization of gems whose induced trisections are genus-minimizing is stated as an open problem.
